model: Bank residual income on tangible book, run as FCFE at cost of equity (engine route; distributable earnings to ordinary shareholders after AT1 coupons less CET1 retention on RWA growth, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E Group net banking income (revenues). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported at the valuation date; FY0 = 1H26 actual 28,147 (BNP.PA_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:835 + Q1-2026.txt:830; +10.2% YoY including the AXA IM scope effect from 1 Jul 2025) plus 2H26 estimated at ~26,850 (2H25 was 25,682; +4.5% YoY, below 1H26 growth because the AXA IM scope effect lapses from 3Q26 and CIB is seasonally softer). FY2025 actual 51,223 (Q4-2025.txt:906). Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, which ends 14 months after the valuation date; the engine discounts it as one full year, a two-month over-discount accepted for simplicity.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,116,784,757 shares issued at 31 Dec 2025 (BNP.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:20020) less 16,685,450 held by the Group (15.9m proprietary from the 2025 buyback awaiting cancellation + 0.8m trading book, :20043) = 1,100.1m outstanding. In 1H26 the statement of changes in equity shows a EUR 1,168m capital reduction (Q2-2026.txt:~1120), i.e. the cancellation of the 15.9m treasury shares, with no share issuance, so ~1,100m remains the outstanding count at 30 Jun 2026. Cross-checks: FY2025 net book value per share 104.3 (Annual FY2025:1770) = (125,513 - 10,614 TSSDI) / 1,100.1 = 104.4; 1H26 EPS 6.45 = (7,562 - 436 TSSDI coupons) / ~1,105m average. The 10%-of-net-income 2026 buyback tranche (~EUR 1.3bn, ~16m shares) had not been launched at the 23 Jul 2026 release; it is funded out of the FCFE the model values, so it is NOT netted off the count (doing both would double-count). Count held FLAT: share-based payment is immaterial and the 60% payout policy plus surplus-CET1 distribution from 2027 is modelled as cash to shareholders, not as share shrinkage.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt held at ZERO by construction. BNP Paribas is an ECB/SSM-supervised G-SIB: customer deposits (EUR 1,093bn at Mar-26, kpis), debt securities and subordinated debt are operating funding whose cost sits inside net banking income; cash and balances at central banks (EUR 213bn at 30 Jun 2026, core_metrics cash_and_equivalents) are liquidity held against that funding (LCR 149%), not surplus. total_debt and cash are deliberately recorded as 0 here so no consumer treats the EUR 213bn as net cash; the actual figures live in core_metrics. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income to ordinary shareholders less capital retained to hold CET1 at 13% as RWA grows), discounted at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE to ordinary shareholders = underlying pre-tax income ~18,150 (33.0% of NBI; 1H26 reported 10,671 less the EUR 858m untaxed Ageas/AGI divestment gain = 9,813, plus 2H26 ~8,340) x (1 - 34.0% tax, minority and AT1-coupon leakage) = 11,979 distributable, less ~2,535 CET1 retention (13% x ~EUR 780bn RWA x ~2.5% RWA growth) = 9,444. Cross-check on the distributable line: FY2025 net income group share 12,225 less TSSDI remuneration 822 (412 + 410, Q2-2026.txt equity statement) = 11,403; +5% = 11,973. Cross-check on retention: CET1 rose 12.6% -> 13.0% in 1H26 while 60% of earnings were distributed, i.e. organic generation ran ~+30bp/quarter net of RWA growth against -20bp of distribution, so true FCFE exceeds the 60% payout; the model's ~79% FY2026E (66% in FY2027 once the output-floor top-up is charged) is the conservative end of that evidence. reported_fcf = last_fcf because SBC and interest income are both zero on this route.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow for a bank is deposit, loan and trading-book movement and is meaningless as free cash flow; the financial-parser left operating_cash_flow and free_cash_flow empty for that reason. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment plans line in the consolidated statement of changes in equity: EUR (8)m in 2H25, EUR 2m in 1H26 (BNP.PA_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt equity statement); BNP Paribas discontinued stock-option and performance-share plans in 2012 and pays deferred variable compensation in cash or index-linked instruments expensed inside operating expenses. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: EUR 1,150m buyback related to 2025 earnings finalised 19 Dec 2025 (Q4-2025.txt:271); 29.2m shares acquired for EUR 2,234m in calendar 2025 (Annual FY2025:20036) spanning the 2024- and 2025-earnings programmes. 2026 policy: 60% payout of which at least 50% dividends and 10% buybacks (Q4-2025.txt:277); from 2027 at least 60% plus distribution of surplus CET1 above 13%, decided annually. Buybacks are one form the modelled FCFE takes, not an additional source of value, so the count is held flat.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:24Z Euronext Paris regular close (Friday 17:37 CEST); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (31 Dec 2025 issued less treasury, carried through the 1H26 cancellation; see share_count_basis)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity group share EUR 131,922m at 30 Jun 2026 (core_metrics; Q2-2026.txt equity statement) less undated super-subordinated notes (TSSDI/AT1) EUR 11,862m = ordinary equity 120,060 = EUR 109.1/share; less goodwill 7,246 and intangibles 4,655 (Q2-2026.txt:1005-1006) = tangible ordinary equity EUR 108,159m = TNBV EUR 98.3/share before the EUR 3.23 interim dividend detached 24 Sep 2026 (3Q26 earnings of ~EUR 2.7/share roughly replace it). Method check: the same arithmetic on 31 Dec 2024 gives 93.9 vs the published revalued TNBV of 93.7 (Q4-2024.txt:204), and on 31 Dec 2025 93.8 vs published 93.50 (Annual FY2025:10160). Price/TNBV at 83.52 = 0.85x; P/NBV 0.77x. ROTE 11.6% FY2025 (Annual FY2025:10164), 13.3% 1H26 including the Ageas gain (~11.8% underlying); guided ~12% 2026, >13% 2028. CET1 13.0% at 30 Jun 2026 (target 13% for 2027-28 met early; SREP 10.43%); RWA EUR 779.5bn and CET1 capital EUR 98.3bn at 31 Dec 2025 (Annual FY2025:26020, :26711); SRT/credit-insurance RWA savings stock EUR 63bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in EUR, the currency of the flows: 10-year Bund ~2.75% (October 2026) + beta 1.3 (large eurozone universal bank with a 36% CIB revenue share) x eurozone equity risk premium 5.6% = 10.0%. One rate across all three scenarios. The French sovereign spread (OAT-Bund >120bp, widest since 2012), funding-cost, credit-cycle and integration risk are charged in the bear flows and in the 30% bear weight, not stacked onto the discount rate. The market price implies a cost of equity of ~13.5% at a 12% ROTE and 2.5% growth ((ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = 0.85x), which the required-return table makes visible.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease interest sit inside operating expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin; lease liabilities are immaterial against EUR 132bn of equity. No lease line, no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. Minority interests (EUR 633m FY2025 = 17,065 pre-tax - 4,207 tax - 12,225 group share; EUR 238m 1H26, Q2-2026.txt:925) are absorbed into the cash_tax_rate driver together with corporate tax and TSSDI coupons: FY2025 tax 24.7% + NCI 3.7% + TSSDI 4.8% = 33.2%; 1H26 ex-gain 29.3% + 2.4% + 4.4% = 36.1% (1Q carries the non-deductible full-year bank levies); FY2026E 34.0%. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book. Run as FCFE at the cost of equity through the component engine, exactly as NAB.AX (2026-09-24) and HSBC (2026-10): residual income on book and FCFE with retention = CET1 x delta-RWA are the same clean-surplus valuation (value = TBV + PV of (ROTE - CoE) x TBV), and the engine route produces the validated JSON, slider engine and workbook. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = Group net banking income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income margin (NBI - operating expenses - cost of risk - cost of legal risk on financial instruments + equity-method and other recurring non-operating items); sbc_pct_path = 0 (SBC-zero); da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation of software and premises is a real cost inside operating expenses, not an add-back); capex_pct_path = regulatory capital RETAINED to hold CET1 at 13% as risk-weighted assets grow (0.13 x RWA/NBI ~14.2x x RWA growth), plus a CRR3 output-floor top-up in FY2027-28 (65% -> 72.5% floor); cash_tax_rate_path = corporate tax + minority interests + TSSDI (AT1) coupons as % of pre-tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0; wc_capture = 0. FY0 reconciliation: 55,000 x 33.0% x (1 - 34%) = 11,979 distributable vs FY2025 actual 12,225 - 822 TSSDI = 11,403 (+5%) and 1H26 underlying (7,562 - 761 exceptional - 436 TSSDI) = 6,365 (annualising to ~12.5bn with 1H seasonality). ONE-OFF: the EUR 858m Ageas/AGI capital gain (2Q26, before and after tax) is excluded from FY0; so is the EUR +13bp CET1 benefit of the divestment cycle (BMCI 67% sale in exclusive talks) which would add to FCFE, not to earnings. SCALE CHECK: all figures EUR millions as in the press-release tables; share count in millions; per-share values in EUR. Price is the Euronext regular close; H1 2026 (30 Jun 2026) is the latest balance sheet; no H1-2026 interim report is in Extracted/ (Q2-2026 press release only), so goodwill, intangibles, TSSDI and equity come from the press-release balance sheet and equity statement.
inputs.sanity_check_caveat: Model label contains 'residual income', 'tangible book', 'cost of equity' and 'distributable earnings' so scripts/sanity_check.py and sectors.bucket() route to bank multiples (P/TBV, P/E), not EV/EBITDA or D/E. Price and all per-share metrics are per ordinary share on Euronext Paris in EUR; no ADR ratio and no FX bridge apply.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is net income group share (TSSDI coupons ~0.8bn/yr are stable, so the CAGR is unaffected): FY2020 7,067 (COVID provisioning trough, cost of risk 5,717); FY2022 10,196; FY2023 10,975; FY2024 11,688; FY2025 12,225 (core_metrics). Revenue (NBI): FY2020 44,275; FY2022 50,419 (includes Bank of the West, sold 1 Feb 2023); FY2023 45,874; FY2025 51,223 - the 3-year revenue CAGR of 0.5% is depressed by the disposal; from the FY2023 post-disposal base NBI compounded 5.7%/yr to FY2025 (AXA IM adds ~2pp of that in FY2025-26). Equity CAGR is held down by design: 50% cash payout plus EUR 0.9-2.2bn/yr of buybacks and the 2023 EUR 5bn extraordinary buyback after Bank of the West.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average net banking income growth (4.0% FY2027 fading to 2.5%), anchored between the 5-year revenue CAGR (3.0%), the post-disposal FY2023-25 revenue CAGR (5.7%) and management's 2025-28 plan (net income >10%/yr, which the base does not grant in full).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3/5-year CAGR (1.0% / 2.2%) diverges >30% from EPS (9.7% / 14.1%) and from net income (6.2% / 11.6%): book value is deliberately held near flat by a 60% payout (dividends plus buybacks) and the EUR 5bn Bank of the West special buyback, and the 5-year EPS CAGR starts from the FY2020 COVID trough. Neither equity nor EPS CAGR describes the earnings-power trend; growth is taken from the revenue and distributable-earnings series.

base.growth_rationale: Net banking income. FY2027 +4.0%: the AXA IM scope effect has fully lapsed by then, CPBS grows ~4% (loan growth +4-5%, deposit reinvestment tailwind fading as ECB rates stabilise), IPS high-single-digit on net inflows and the AXA distribution partnership, CIB mid-single-digit after an exceptional 2026 (+12%). Tapers to 2.5% terminal (eurozone nominal GDP ~3.5% less structural NIM compression and Arval/used-car cyclicality). Management's plan implies ~5% revenue growth to 2028; the base grants 4%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income on NBI. FY2026E underlying 33.0% = 100 - cost/income 60.5 - cost of risk 6.3 (~37bp) - legal risk 0.6 + recurring non-operating 1.4 (equity-method incl. Ageas 22.5%, dividends). FY2027 33.8% / FY2029 35.2%: cost/income improves ~1pt/yr to ~58% by 2029 (management targets <56% by 2028; FY2025 61.2%, 1H26 59.3%) as AXA IM synergies and the AI-driven support-function plan land, offset by cost of risk normalising from ~37bp to 40-42bp (6.8-7.0% of NBI). Mature 35.0% = 100 - 58.0 - 7.0 - 0.6 + 0.6. FY2025 actual was 33.3% (17,065 / 51,223).
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at 13% = 0.13 x RWA/NBI (14.2x in FY2026E, drifting to ~13.4x as fee-based NBI outgrows RWA) x RWA growth, with RWA growing 1pt slower than NBI (management guides ~+2%/yr organic incl. securitisations; the base uses 3.0% in FY2027-28, 2.5%, then 2.0%, and RWA = NBI growth of 2.5% in the terminal years because RWA cannot lag revenue forever). FY2027-28 carry an extra ~EUR 1.3bn/yr (2.3% of NBI) for the CRR3 output-floor step from 65% to 72.5% net of SRT mitigation. At 4% growth 7.5% of NBI (~EUR 4.3bn, 34% of distributable earnings retained -> 66% paid out, in line with the >=60% policy); at 2.5% terminal growth 4.4% (~22% retained -> 78% paid out, which is the 60% payout plus the surplus-CET1 distribution promised from 2027).
base.tax_rationale: Corporate tax ~29% of pre-tax (FY2025 24.7% flattered by the untaxed Ageas dividend and equity-method income; 1H26 ex-gain 29.3%) + minority interests ~2.5% (BNL/BGL/Türkiye/Cardif partners) + TSSDI (AT1) coupons ~4.8% (EUR 436m in 1H26, EUR 822m FY2025, stock EUR 11.9bn after the EUR 1.25bn 1H26 issue) = ~36% near term, 34.0% through the horizon as the AT1 stock grows slower than pre-tax income. The AT1 coupon is a real cost to ordinary shareholders charged to equity, not P&L, and is deducted here exactly once.

bull.growth_rationale: The 2025-28 plan is delivered: CIB keeps taking EMEA share (DCM/ECM/M&A league tables, prime services), IPS compounds at 8-10% on AXA IM cross-selling and the Savings & Investments Union retail-savings shift, CPBS grows 4-5% as eurozone loan demand recovers. NBI +5.5% FY2027 fading to 3% terminal; net income to ordinary grows >10%/yr to 2028 as management targets.
bull.margin_rationale: Cost/income reaches <56% by 2028 as guided (AXA IM synergies, AI-driven support-function plan, positive jaws every year) and cost of risk holds at ~35bp (5.8% of NBI): 100 - 56.0 - 5.8 - 0.4 + 0.7 = 38.5. ROTE ~14% by 2028, above the >13% target.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = 0.13 x RWA/NBI x RWA growth with RWA growing 1.5pt slower than NBI (faster shift to capital-light IPS/fee revenue, more SRT), plus the same output-floor top-up in FY2027-28; terminal years at RWA growth = 3.0%. Higher growth needs more capital even with a higher ROTE.

bear.growth_rationale: French political and fiscal stress crystallises around the 2027 budget and presidential election: the OAT-Bund spread goes past 200bp, wholesale funding costs rise for all French banks, the eurozone slows, CIB markets revenue and Arval/leasing fall, deposit margins compress on ECB cuts. NBI flat in FY2027, +1% in FY2028, then 2%/yr with no catch-up.
bear.margin_rationale: FY2027: cost/income 63% (negative jaws, integration overruns of the type seen in 1H26 IPS opex +33.7%), cost of risk 60bp (~10% of NBI; FY2020 was 5.7bn/13% of NBI), legal/conduct 1%: 100 - 63 - 10 - 1 + 1 = 27. Recovers only to cost/income 61% and cost of risk 50bp (8%): 100 - 61 - 8 - 0.7 + 1.2 = 31.5, i.e. FY2023-24 profitability without the planned efficiency gains. ROTE settles ~9.5%, at or below the cost of equity, so the franchise is worth about tangible book.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention held at 6.0% of NBI in FY2027-28 despite zero revenue growth: IRB rating migration in a downturn and the output-floor step inflate RWA (~+3%/yr) and the 13% CET1 target is non-negotiable for a G-SIB under ECB supervision, so earnings are retained rather than distributed (the 2020 precedent: dividends suspended by ECB recommendation). Thereafter 0.13 x RWA/NBI ~14.5x x 2% = 3.8%.
bear.tax_rationale: Leakage rises to 36%: bank levies and the TSSDI coupon (~EUR 0.9bn) are fixed against a smaller pre-tax base, and a French corporate surtax of the 2025-26 type recurs.

scenario_narratives.base: BNP Paribas compounds net banking income at 4% fading to 2.5%, lifts pre-tax margin from 33% to 35% as cost/income drifts toward 58% and cost of risk normalises to ~40bp, and holds CET1 at 13% while RWA grows a point slower than revenue. Distributable earnings to ordinary shareholders (after ~EUR 0.9bn of AT1 coupons) rise from ~EUR 12.0bn in FY2026 to ~EUR 12.8bn in FY2027 and ~EUR 19bn by FY2036, of which two-thirds to four-fifths is paid out. At a 10% EUR cost of equity and a ~12-12.7% return on tangible equity the franchise is worth ~1.35x tangible book of EUR 98/share; the market pays 0.85x, which is consistent with a ~13.5% cost of equity or a belief that ROTE reverts to single digits.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-28 plan lands in full: cost/income below 56% by 2028, cost of risk ~35bp, CIB share gains and the AXA IM platform push IPS to high-single-digit growth, net income to ordinary compounds >10% a year to 2028 and ROTE reaches ~14%. Surplus CET1 above 13% is returned annually from 2027 on top of the 60% payout. Worth ~1.7-1.8x tangible book at a 10% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: A French sovereign-spread shock around the 2027 election raises funding costs, the eurozone slips into recession, cost of risk runs at 60bp for two years, CIB and Arval revenues fall, integration costs overrun and the ECB leans on distributions while the output floor inflates RWA. Revenue stalls for two years, cost/income sticks above 60%, ROTE settles ~9.5% - at the cost of equity - and the franchise is worth roughly tangible book, with the 2020-style dividend suspension as the template for how shareholders experience it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear doubled to 30%: the Analysis grades French political/fiscal risk 'high' (OAT-Bund spread widest since 2012 in September 2026, 2027 budget and presidential election ahead), three large integrations run simultaneously (AXA IM, HSBC Germany, Ageas/AG Insurance), Arval is already in a used-car downcycle, and the output-floor phase-in to 2028 is a known capital headwind; the market at 0.85x tangible book is itself a vote for the bear path. Bull cut to 20%: it requires the full 2028 plan (cost/income <56%, ROTE >13%) to be delivered with a benign credit cycle and a re-rating of European bank multiples that has not happened in fifteen years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A universal bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a cost of equity in the currency of its earnings - never on statutory operating cash flow (deposit and trading-book movement) and never with deposits or debt securities treated as net debt. Net income to ordinary shareholders after AT1 coupons is the flow; CET1 retention on RWA growth is the reinvestment; 10% is the return an owner of EUR bank equity requires. This is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: value = tangible book + PV of the spread between ROTE and the cost of equity. BNP earns ~12% on EUR 98/share of tangible book and trades at 0.85x it; the model says that discount prices in either a sustained French funding shock or a cost of equity in the mid-teens, and the weighted value sits well above the price even with the bear case at 30%. The result is not a call on when the European bank discount closes.
key_risks_to_valuation: French sovereign spread: BNP is one of the largest wholesale issuers in the EU; a sustained OAT-Bund spread >150bp lifts funding costs and MREL issuance costs and would push cost/income and capital-ratio volatility toward the bear path
Cost of risk: every 10bp on ~EUR 940bn of customer loans is ~EUR 0.94bn pre-tax (~5% of pre-tax income); 1H26 ran at 39bp against <40bp guidance, 2020 ran at 66bp
Cost/income delivery: the base assumes ~58% by 2029 against management's <56% by 2028; each point of cost/income is ~EUR 0.55bn pre-tax (~3%)

Regulatory capital: the CRR3 output floor (65% in 2026 -> 72.5% in 2028), FRTB and any SREP add-on raise retention above the modelled 0.13 x delta-RWA; SRT/credit-insurance savings (EUR 63bn RWA) depend on market capacity

Share count: the ~1,100m count is derived (issued less treasury, carried through the 1H26 cancellation), not read from an interim report; the FY2026 URD (March 2027) will print the year-end count and the 2026 buyback tranche
Integration: AXA IM (EUR 5.4bn), HSBC Germany private banking and the Ageas/AG Insurance restructuring are being absorbed at once; 1H26 IPS opex +33.7% YoY shows the cost base is still moving
Rates: eurozone deposit reinvestment is a tailwind that fades as the ECB cycle ends; 5bp of NIM on ~EUR 1.1tn of deposits/loans is ~EUR 0.5bn of NBI (~1%)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (Euronext Paris regular close); 52-week range 65.12-113.82.

TSSDI and coupons (1060-1160); FY2025 Universal Registration Document (BNP.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt) key figures incl. NBV per share (1766-1790), ROTE/TNBV (10160-10196), share capital and treasury shares (20020-20048), RWA and CET1 capital (26020, 26711).
data_sources.qualitative: BNP.PA_Analysis.json (2026-10-25): integrated three-division model, AXA IM / HSBC Germany / Ageas transactions, 2025-28 targets (ROTE 12% 2026, >13% 2028; cost/income ~60% then <56%; net income >10%/yr), French political risk and OAT-Bund spread, Arval downcycle, CRR3 output floor, 2027-2030 plan due February 2027, analyst target cuts (Kepler, Alphavalue) in October 2026.
